rv.q: But, in general, the play is flabbily written and displays an ageing writer's disdain for the kind of sexual pleasures he once joyously advocated.
It may well be, but it’s not nearly as vital or funny or true: it’s as though Coward dumped the public persona that defined his style and his glamour and wrote a play that anyone else might write.

cn.t: Coward's long-rejected 1956 play receives a tepid West End premiere, with critics finding modest interest in the tropical melodrama but little to justify its resurrection from obscurity.
